title: Can some one creat this?
author: Abject-Average-7641
selftext: So I have an idea for a game but I don't have access to a computer and only have a cheap phone with limited access to the internet. The game idea is an invention game where you can creat your own things (like mechs,cars, tanks,etc). You have a garage/hanger where you have a 3d view of your invention,can look around and use a large variety of parts (pistons,wheels,grips,cables, conveyor belts,etc...) and are each a block big (like Minecraft), you also have nodes and wires (like in terraria that interact with parts but don't take up space). All of that is in the "creating room". After you can rest it outside the creating room and can bake or borrow your own world. For low quality mobile phones in can be tested on a 2d world,but your inventions can spin around and go up or down. If you are playing in a PC, console or good phone it is 3, (kind of like dayZ mobile view). It is just an idea if some one would like to use it, I don't have money so yeah. I you have any questions I'll try to answer it. I'm new to reddit and this is my first post or whatever you call it, so yeah, thank you for reading this.👍

comments.author: erofamiliar
comments.body:
So, I genuinely don't want to be mean. Please forgive me if any of this sounds harsh, I don't mean to put a damper on your enthusiasm. Gamedev is really cool and I understand the desire to put your ideas out there, hoping someone with more experience bites. However, the "idea guy" is a meme in a lot of creative communities for a reason.

Every individual thing you've suggested is very difficult for experienced teams of developers with years of industry experience. Put together, you're basically suggesting Minecraft + Gmod + BeamNG + Kerbal Space Program, all merged into one, in a world that could be procedurally generated, that can run in both 3D and 2D, that runs on mobile phones. I'd recommend taking a look at something like Besiege, which has only a few of the elements you suggest, but still spent five years in early access.

On top of it being unfeasible, I'm not sure what the goal would be either, beyond creating things.  In many creative games, your creations serve some kind of purpose. The idea of "a game where you make things" is not one that has enough of a hook for anyone to seriously consider.

My recommendation would be to download something small, like Godot, for your phone. You can develop Godot games on Android, and trying to make a very simple project should help you understand how complex even "simple" elements are. It's also worth doing some research on what game designers do.

Maybe you could refine this into something that excites you enough to work on it yourself? Everyone has to start somewhere. Every gamedev starts with a crazy dream game, is confused that nobody wants to take a crack at it, and then has to dive in to understand why. In doing so, you'll come to learn what is actually feasible. Hopefully.
